habitat_short.text: Moderately clear to turbid, quiet warm water with vegetation, logs, trees, brush, stumps and underwater contours.
habitat_short.quote: Moderately clear to turbid, quiet warm waters in streams, rivers, lakes, reservoirs and ponds. Vegetation, near logs, trees, brush, stumps and underwater contours.

temp_preferred_f.source_title: Habitat Suitability Index Models: Largemouth Bass (Stuber, Gebhart, Maughan; USFWS FWS/OBS-82/10.16, 1982)
temp_preferred_f.quote: Optimal temperatures for growth of adult bass range from 24-30° C
temp_preferred_f.note: Original in Celsius: 24-30 C = 75-86 F. USFWS HSI FWS/OBS-82/10.16 (Stuber et al. 1982).

temp_spawn_f.quote: but most occurs between 16 and 22° C
temp_spawn_f.note: Original in Celsius: 16-22 C = 61-72 F (HSI). TPWD says spawning begins about 60 F.

spawn_months_tx.quote: This can occur as early as February or as late as May, depending on where one is in the state.
spawn_months_tx.label: Feb to May, depending on where in Texas

baits.technique: Fish move into shallows to spawn; big females near spawning areas in March.
baits.quote: March is the best time to catch a trophy-size bass.

baits.bait: Topwater baits in low light; spinnerbaits, hard-body lures, plastic worms later in the day
baits.technique: Topwater at dawn/dusk, then switch to subsurface lures.
baits.quote: Many anglers use top-water baits in low-light conditions and switch to spinner baits, hard-body lures or plastic worms

baits.technique: By June bass start moving deeper.
baits.quote: By June, they start moving into deeper water.

baits.bait: Crankbaits, spinnerbaits, jigs, soft plastics, spoons, minnows, earthworms, crawfish
baits.technique: General TPWD list.
baits.quote: Crankbaits, spinner baits, jigs, soft plastics, spoons, flies, minnows, earthworms, crawfish, leeches, frogs, lizards and insects.

regs_statewide.daily_bag: 5 (combined with smallmouth, Alabama, Guadalupe and spotted bass)

habitat_short.text: Open water of large streams, rivers and reservoirs; adults feed on shad; spawning run up tributaries over gravel or rock.

temp_preferred_f.kind: preferred (field selection near power-plant effluent, Gammon 1973, as cited in HSI)

spawn_months_tx.label: runs start Feb-Mar, done by May

activity.quote_2: look for schooling fish at dawn or on cloudy days

baits.bait: Jigs, spinners, soft plastic shad, small crankbaits
baits.technique: Spawning run in tributaries after rain.
baits.quote: Popular lures for the spawning season include jigs, spinners, soft plastic shad and small crank baits.

baits.technique: Dead bait on bottom; live bait at any depth.
baits.quote: Dead bait should be fished on the bottom while live bait can be fished at any depth.

baits.technique: Find birds diving over surfacing schools.
baits.quote: Crank baits, soft plastic shad and topwater baits are good at these times.

baits.bait: Natural baits, slabs, jigs under a light

habitat_short.text: Reservoir fish that depend on stocking in most Texas lakes (Lake Texoma is an exception); feeds mainly on shad.

reproduction.text: Texas hybrids are hatchery fish. TPWD says only white bass reproduce in significant numbers in Central Texas; hybrid populations depend on stocking. CONFLICT: Texas A&M page says hybrids are fertile; TPWD Jim Chapman page says they do not reproduce. For the engine: treat as stocked fish, no spawn window.

sources.quote: Central Texas striped bass and hybrid striped bass populations are completely supported from stockings by Texas Parks and Wildlife Department fish hatcheries.
because hybrid striped bass do not reproduce, they are stocked annually by TPWD to maintain the fishery
they are fertile, unlike most other hybrid species

habitat_short.text: Schools around submerged trees, docks and other structure; black crappie common in clear east Texas waters.

habitat_short.quote: Channel catfish are most abundant in large streams with low or moderate current.
